## Goal

Agents start from excellent templates, people see what Mostra can do at a glance and can try it with one prompt to their agent, and the docs describe the released version wherever they are read.

## Scope

From [WORK_PACKAGES.md](../WORK_PACKAGES.md):

- `mostra new` templates for every family, one-off and long-lived (questionnaire, proposal, prototype or review, dashboard, deck, demo, inbox, tasks, custom), each with AGENTS.md, including a team (roster) form and a hosted-sharing example;
- the gallery (prompt, source and result side by side, including the launch demos), on the docs site, with a selection on the project site; each entry can be copied by an agent to use as is or build on;
- the docs site, built with a standard static docs generator (generated references, per-page Markdown, `llms.txt`) and served at `docs.mostradev.com` by its own Cloudflare Worker from the release workflow, covering remote servers, the relay, teams and the telemetry event list;
- an SPA first-class review across the codebase.

Design detail for this package:

- From MT-04 (D174): the docs site and the gallery link the showcase walkthrough (the Skill's `references/walkthrough.md` and the project site's `walkthrough.md`), and WP-26 runs its hosted path if MT-04 recorded it as untested.
- From WP-14 (D162): the Skill's three examples (`skills/mostra/assets/examples/`) seed the templates and the gallery; when `mostra new --template` exists, the Skill's step 2 and the scaffolded `AGENTS.md` (`packages/runtime/src/publish/scaffold.ts`) name it. Links from the Skill and the plugin's README to docs pages move to the docs site once it is deployed, and the plugin's `homepage` and `documentationUrl` in `tools/plugins/definition.ts` with them (the directory listing shows both).
- Templates per family, one-off and long-lived, each with AGENTS.md and passing verify; they include a team (roster) form and a hosted-sharing example (D121, D116).
- Gallery with prompt, source and result, including the launch demos. Each entry shows a capture (from the CI baselines, so it is current with every release), the prompt that made it with a copy button, the source, and "Make one like this": a prompt that has the reader's agent copy the entry as its starting point (through `mostra new --template` where the entry is a template, otherwise its source), to use as is or build on. Entries whose point is answering also open live: a hosted page each visitor answers on their own copy. The full gallery lives on the docs site; the project site shows a selection. At first the gallery holds the project's own entries and those of early users who agree; contributions by pull request, checked by `verify` in CI like every example, come next; publishing from the hosted service comes later. *Why:* anyone who sees a page should understand what Mostra does and be able to try it with one prompt, and an agent starts best from a page that already passes `verify`.
- Docs site built with a standard static docs generator, not as Mostra pages (Astro Starlight fits: its current release supports the project site's Astro and has a maintained `llms.txt` plugin, with built-in search, navigation and sitemaps), with generated references, per-page Markdown and `llms.txt`; it covers remote servers, the relay, teams and the public telemetry event list (D119). It is served at `docs.mostradev.com` by its own Cloudflare Worker (static assets), deployed by the release workflow on each release tag with a deploy token limited to that Worker, and a preview from `main` that isn't listed or indexed. `DEFAULT_DOCS_BASE` and the plugin's `documentationUrl` move to the new address; the GitHub Pages address (`mostra-dev.github.io/mostra`) keeps serving a redirect for every path to the same path on the new address, so diagnostics' links in released versions keep resolving (D37). The Worker sends a Markdown content type for the per-page Markdown, redirects for moved pages and the site's security headers. *Why:* the docs stay up independently of any hosted service, describe the version people can install, and get search, navigation and versioning from a maintained generator; GitHub Pages can't set headers or redirects.
- If the kit's registry (WP-18) is public in shadcn's registry format, it is listed in shadcn's Registry Directory when the project launches.
- SPA-mode completeness review (RS-02).
- The hosted service is labelled "beta" in the docs: the docs site, the pages for `mostra share --cloud` and for remote servers, and the remote MCP server's description say so, until its paid plans are generally available, when the label comes off in one change. *Why:* it sets expectations for a new hosted service while it is still free to use.
- The official MCP Registry can list Mostra: `@mostra/cli`'s `package.json` carries `"mcpName": "com.mostradev/mostra"` in a published release, and the repository gains a `server.json` for the registry under the same name describing both ways to run the server: the npm package (`npx -y @mostra/cli mcp`, stdio) and the hosted server's remote MCP endpoint (Streamable HTTP, OAuth). The name is proven by a DNS TXT record on `mostradev.com` (the registry's domain verification); publishing the entry is a release step. *Why:* the registry, which other directories and clients read, verifies that whoever publishes an npm-based entry owns the package by reading `mcpName` from the published `package.json`, and a reverse-DNS name on the project's domain is the one an organization can prove without a person's GitHub account.
